es.title: Las gasolineras independientes buscan refugio en las marcas ante la deriva de precios del combustible
es.description: La deriva de precios que arrastran los combustibles a lo largo de este año comienza a hacer mella entre los pequeños y medianos empresarios de estaciones de servicio que están llegando con el agua al cuello al final del ejercicio ante la imposibilidad de competir con las grandes marcas para atraer a clientes en un contexto marcado por los costes récord de diésel y gasolina . Ante esta coyuntura, una parte de esas sociedades -la mayoría, pymes o empresas familiares- están buscando refugio en algunas de las redes de gasolineras o bien negociando fórmulas de unión para evitar caer en la quiebra técnica. Esa es la circunstancia por la que atraviesa parte del sector de las estaciones de servicio después de ocho meses desde que se iniciaran los ataques estadounidenses sobre Irán. Un acontecimiento geopolítico que está impactando en las cuentas de muchas pequeñas sociedades por el elevado coste del combustible y la imposibilidad de ofrecer los descuentos que las grandes redes llevan aplicando desde marzo. Aunque esa búsqueda de integración no cesa, la realidad es que las redes comerciales de mayor implantación no están incluyendo nuevas franquicias, tal y como apuntan varias fuentes consultadas en el sector energético y petrolífero. La fortaleza de las estaciones de servicio independientes, marca blanca o sin adscripción comercial, se ha convertido ahora en su principal vulnerabilidad . Las rebajas de precios -'low cost', como se conoce a muchas de estas instalaciones popularmente- les permitía competir con las marcas históricas mientras los costes estaban moderados. Ajustaban sus márgenes y atraían a clientes. Pero la deriva del combustible actual ha supuesto un punto de inflexión para sus cuentas de resultados: tienen que pagar la materia prima muy cara y no son capaces de venderla con descuentos sin que vean dañados sus negocios, indican esas mismas fuentes. Los movimientos corporativos para «cobijarse» en algún paraguas , léase una red de estaciones de servicio, se han reproducido en los últimos meses. Y lo han hecho sobre todo los empresarios del ámbito rural, donde este tipo de gasolineras independientes son mucho más frecuentes que el resto. Estos negocios se han quedado sin margen de actuación y ven cómo los precios que ofrecen al consumidor son ahora más caros que en Repsol, Moeve o BP, las firmas más reconocidas del sector petrolífero en España. La proliferación de gasolineras sin marca les llevó a acaparar un 44% de la red de estaciones de servicio, en muchos casos por parte de empresarios ajenos al sector energéticoDe las 12.746 estaciones de servicio que hay en todo el país, según los datos actualizados de AICE, el 46% pertenecen a algunas de sus asociadas (Repsol, Moeve, BP y Saras). Un 10% se aglutinan en torno a otros operadores. Pero el 44% restante son identificadas como independientes. Su evolución ha sido tan alcista que en apenas 15 años han llegado a duplicar la cuota de mercado que tenían en 2011, restándole protagonismo a las grandes. Pero con la guerra de Irán y la explosión de precios, el mercado de muchas de ellas se encuentra completamente roto. En el sector reconocen que buena parte de estos negocios fueron inaugurados o comprados por empresarios que no provenían precisamente de la energía , sino que vieron una oportunidad en su momento. Pero ahora, en un contexto en el que los números no les dan, tienen menos herramientas para competir y se ven «en terreno de nadie», apunta un importante empresario regional a ABC. Y ante esta circunstancia, las grandes no quieren asumir más estaciones de servicio tanto por la estructura vertical de sus negocios como por las propias limitaciones de cuota de mercado que les impone la ley de 2015 y que quería evitar grandes concentraciones. Además, las independientes cuentan con otro hándicap que ha ido mermándoles en los últimos años: la proliferación de normativas tanto medioambientales como de distribución y permisos de operación, ante los que también se encuentran presionados. Varias fuentes indican que hay más de 100 normas en vigor que todas deben cumplir -unas 40 estatales y otras 60 autonómicas- que van mermando sus estructuras y que, ahora más que antes, también les impulsa a intentar integrarse en alguna red. Pero en la mayoría de los casos lo hacen sin resultado. 60 Normas autonómicas La regulación medioambiental, de permisos e instalaciones fagotiza a buena parte del sector al implantar o mantener este tipo de negociosLa deriva que han tomado los precios de la gasolina y el diésel en los últimos meses ha provocado varios choques con respecto a lo que ocurría en las gasolineras antes de esta crisis. Por ejemplo, que las estaciones de servicio independiente fueron las que más subieron los precios, proporcionalmente hablando, con respecto a lo que hicieron las grandes marcas. Eso ocurrió en marzo, cuando los descuentos por fidelización de Waylet, Moeve Go o Mi BP comenzaron a implantarse en sus respectivas marcas. Un fin de año vertiginosoLa brecha de precios que siempre ha existido entre las grandes petroleras y el resto de independientes se ha ido estrechando a lo largo de los últimos meses. A finales de octubre, tomando como referencia los precios de venta del día 29, la diferencia entre la marca más cara de gasolina y las que no están asociadas a ninguna red era de apenas ocho céntimos de euro, y ello sin contar las rebajas derivadas de los programas de fidelización. En el caso del diésel, esa distancia apenas era de diez céntimos de euro, según los datos extraídos del geoportal del Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica. A esta situación llega el mercado ante un mes de noviembre en el que el Gobierno mantendrá el descuento de 20 céntimos por litro tanto para la gasolina como para el diésel, después de que los carburantes subiese más de un 15% en septiembre en comparación con el año anterior tal y como ha sucedido según los datos de inflación publicados este miércoles por el INE. Concretamente, el gasóleo se ha encarecido en septiembre un 34% y la gasolina un 27,5%. El gasóleo de automoción iniciará el mes, de nuevo, por encima de los 1,90 euros, y la gasolina 95, en los 1,74 euros.

es.title: El precio de la gasolina y el diésel desde hoy: así quedan las ayudas y el coste de llenar el depósito
es.description: Durante este puente se van a producir más de cinco millones de desplazamientos, según las estimaciones de la DGT. Se trata de una nueva operación especial que se verá condicionada también por los precios del carburante. Desde que se inició la guerra en Irán, la gasolina y el diésel han presionado al alza, con el consiguiente repunte de la inflación, lo que ha provocado que el Gobierno tuviera que tomar medidas para aliviar el impacto en el bolsillo de los consumidores. En el primer paquete de medidas la decisión supuso rebajar el IVA del 21 al 10% . Con el toque de atención de Bruselas, el Ejecutivo cambió la estrategia y decidió apostar por una rebaja gradual sobre el Impuesto de Hidrocarburos condicionada a la evolución de la inflación. Esa es la fórmula que hoy sigue en pie. Las ayudas a los combustibles las condiciona el IPC. El dato adelantado de octubre se ha situado en el 4,9% . El INE señala que en la estimación «destaca la influencia a la baja de los combustibles y carburantes para vehículos personales». Con todo, este dato no nos permite conocer con exactitud en cuánto se sitúa la inflación tanto del diésel como la de gasolina. Por eso, el dato de referencia para saber si las ayudas se mantienen o se rebajan es el del IPC definitivo publicado a principios de octubre sobre el cierre de septiembre. La variación anual de la inflación del gasóleo se situó en el 34% mientras que la de la gasolina se encuentra en el 27,5%.Ambos datos se sitúan por encima del 15% de inflación respecto al mes anterior que prevé el decreto. Por este motivo, la ayuda de 20 céntimos sobre el decreto de hidrocarburos se mantiene durante el mes de noviembre. La ayuda al diésel y a la gasolina se mantiene en 20 céntimos en noviembreEl precio del diésel y la gasolina: lo que te cuesta llenar el depósito hoyA pesar de que las ayudas han contribuido a que el impacto del precio de los carburantes sobre el bolsillo no sea tan fuerte, repostar hoy sigue siendo más caro que hace un año. La gasolina cuesta de media hoy en España 1,737 euros por litro. Esto implica que llenar un depósito medio vale 86,85 euros . El diésel roza los dos euros: cuesta 1,910 euros . Por ello, llenar el tanque supondrá unos 95,5 euros. A principios de octubre de 2025, llenar un depósito de diésel costaba 77,60 euros y uno de gasolina se situaba en los 81,51 euros.86,85 euros el depósito de gasolina El coste medio del litro de gasolina se sitúa en España en los 1,737 euros95,5 euros el depósito de diésel El coste medio del litro de diésel se sitúa en España en los 1,910 eurosCuál sería el precio del combustible sin ayudasDesde que comenzó la guerra en Irán, el precio del combustible no ha dejado de crecer ya que dependen en buena medida de la evolución del crudo, el coste de la matería prima o la logística, así como de su cotización específica. Si la IPC del diésel o de la gasolina baja de ese 15%, el decreto del Gobierno plantea la reducción progresiva de la ayuda a 13 céntimos el primer mes y a seis el siguiente. Con las medidas aplicadas y la evolución del mercado, los combustibles se mantiene hoy más alejados de la barrera de los dos euros, que se llegó a alcanzar a las pocas semanas del inicio de la guerra. En caso de que no se aplicasen medidas, los cálculos de la Confederación Española de Empresarios de Estaciones de Servicio sitúan el litro de gasolina en 1,99 euros y el diésel en 2,14, superando ese límite.

ph.title: London police arrest 139 people outside US Embassy for supporting banned pro-Palestinian group
ph.description: LONDON (AP) — London police said they arrested 139 people at a protest outside the U.S. Embassy on Saturday in support of the banned group Palestine Action. The majority of those taken into custody had expressed support for a proscribed organization, London's Metropolitan Police said in a statement. It said that more arrests are expected as officers remain at the scene. Many of those protesting were retirees and had been holding signs reading: "I oppose genocide, I support Palestine Action." One protester climbed a tree outside the embassy and could be seen waving a placard reading "God help us. Teachers who support Palestine. Palestine Action." More than 4,000 people have been detained since July 2025 for defying the ban, said Defend Our Juries, an activist organization that planned the demonstration. "It is truly dystopian that there have now been over 4,000 arrests under terror laws for peaceful vigils silently expressing opposition to genocide and support for the protest group Palestine Action," the group said. The U.K. government outlawed the direct-action protest group last year as a terrorist organization. The ban makes membership in or support for Palestine Action a crime punishable by up to 14 years in prison. Demonstrators also held a vigil in support of Palestine Action outside the U.S. Consulate in Edinburgh, Scotland, holding placards akin to those in London. No arrests were reported there, but Police Scotland said that inquiries to identify people seen wearing T-shirts and holding banners showing support for a proscribed organization were ongoing. "Evidence is being reviewed and further action will be taken as appropriate," it said. The protests came before an appeal on Nov. 4 at the Supreme Court against Palestine Action's designation as a terror group. Supporters say the ban is draconian and that it violates their freedom of speech. In August, the U.S. government announced sanctions against Palestine Action, designating it as a terror group. Palestine Action, founded in 2020, aims to stop U.K. military support for Israel, which it says is committing genocide against the Palestinians — an accusation that Israel strongly denies. The group says it aims to stop genocide by disrupting "corporate enablers of the Israeli military-industrial complex." In 2024, its activists broke into a factory owned by Israeli weapons manufacturer Elbit Systems UK, smashing equipment with sledgehammers and crowbars. In June 2025, activists broke into a Royal Air Force base, sprayed red paint into the engines of two tanker planes and caused further damage with crowbars.

ph.title: The French Film Festival is a young 29!
ph.description: It’s hard to believe, but the French Film Festival (FFF) 2026 that will commence on November 6, until November 30, is already the 29th iteration of this well-loved filmfest. The SM Cinemas at SM Aura BGC and SM City Manila, the Alliance Francaise de Manille, the Cinematheque Centre, Intramuros, the QCinema at Gateway, and the Likha Filipino Exhibition Hall, will be the venues where these films will be shown this year. This wonderful exchange of culture, values, and people via the medium of cinema is a shared experience that both the French and the Filipino enjoy tremendously; and while the public may not be aware, there is so much cooperation being done between these two nations in the arena of film production - both from a technical and financial perspective. And for SM Cinemas, this is the 4th year, that they’re the commercial ‘home’ for the French Film Festival - with films running from November 6-15. For this year, the focus is on films that showcase Literature, History, Feminism, and Animation. And there’s truly so much to get excited about that one should head to their French Embassy social media pages on FB and IG to peruse the full schedule. As the Ambassador of France to the Philippines Donatienne Hissard said, “Cinema is a language that does not need translation. It has the power to make audiences feel, reflect, and experience new worlds and perspectives. With this year’s selection of titles, we hope to bring the best of French cinema for the Filipino audience to enjoy, and to continue building bridges between our cultures.” Of Literature, there are two new non-musical cinematic interpretations of the classics "Phantom of the Opera" (2026) and "Les Miserables" (2026). Phantom has Deva Cassel in the cast, the daughter of Monica Bellucci and Vincent Cassel. Two modern French novels, "Jalouse" (2017) and "La Delicatesse" (2011) got film adaptations, and the writer/director David Foenkinos arrives for a special screening on November 27 at SM Aura BGC. When it comes to History, the two part historical biopic on Charles de Gaulle (2026) will surely dominate the conversation. The first part deals with World War II, the Fall of Paris in 1940, and the Resistance, and Part 2 deals with preserving Liberté, 1944, and shaping the course of modern European history. And there’s a biopic on Jean Moulin (2026), who led the Resistance movement, while de Gaulle was in London, and was captured and tortured by Gestapo Chief Klaus Barbie. "Onoda" (2021) is a French produced film about the Japanese soldier who was stationed in Lubang Island, Philippines in 1944, and refused to believe the War had ended until he was finally convinced in 1974. For Feminism, look out primarily for the films "La Maison des Femmes" (2025), "L’objet de Delit" (2026), and "Maria" (2024). Maison is about the pioneering center for women survivors of violence. L’Objet follows an opera production and allegation of sexual assault. And Maria is the biopic of Maria Schneider and her controversial and traumatic "Last Tango in Paris experience," the film directed by Bertolucci, that starred Marlon Brando. Animation has films such as "Mu Yi" (2026), which combines Chinese mythology with hand drawn animation. "La vie de Chateau" (2025) is about an 8-year old girl who loses her parents and goes to live with her uncle, a maintenance worker at the Palace of Versailles. Panel discussions for De Gaulle with historians, and for L’Objet de Délit with women civic groups are planned for after their screenings - check the full schedule to know which ones. QCinema Selection include the following French entries - "L’Inconnue" which stars Lea Seydoux, the queer film "Flesh and Fuel," "Diary of a Chambermaid," and "La Gradiva." These are all 2026 films. If there’s one takeaway from this article, it would be that the line-up of this year’s French Film Festival is truly exemplary, and there are many treasures to be viewed. Happy watching, and enjoy the sub-titles!

ph.title: Maui's Bernd Roediger Charges Into World Title Contention on His Home Waves
ph.description: Pro Men's Finalists 2026 Aloha Classic 2026 Aloha Classic Pro Men's Winners L-R Bernd Roediger, Marc Pare-Rico, Antoine Martin, Morgan Noireaux Photo Credit Fish Bowl Diaries Pro Mens Podium Pro Men's Podium Winners at the 2026 Aloha Classic. L-R Bernd Roediger, Marc Pare-Rico, Antoine Martin. Credit: Fish Bowl Diaries Angela Cochrane aerial Angela Cochrane aerial Photo Credit Fish Bowl Diaries One of the world's most celebrated wave riders finishes just 0.05 points from victory at windsurfing's most prestigious event, setting up his first real shot at a world title in Chile next month. HO'OKIPA, Hawaii, Oct. 31, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- American windsurfer Bernd Roediger, who grew up riding the waves of Maui, has finished second at the Aloha Classic in Hawaii, missing out on victory by just 0.05 points. The result moves him up to third in the world rankings, with just one event left in the season. Now in its 43rd year, the Aloha Classic is the most prestigious event in wave windsurfing: the place where the world's best riders invent, refine and showcase the sport's most spectacular moves. Riders use waves as launch ramps for aerial spins and flips, scored by a judging panel much like surfing. A big-wave star's first real title shot Roediger is regarded by many as one of the best wave riders in the world. A multiple Aloha Classic winner, he has won two events in huge waves this season, in Fiji and at the Maui Pro in April. Yet this is the first time he has been in genuine contention for a world wave title. The reason is a sport that has reinvented itself. Earlier this year, professional windsurfing's two rival circuits, the long-established Professional Windsurfing Association and the breakaway International Windsurfing Tour, merged to form a single World Windsurf Tour. The unified tour has expanded beyond its traditional European base to big-wave venues in Hawaii, Fiji, Australia and Chile. A new five-star event system means every competition now counts towards the world rankings. For riders like Roediger, who excel in powerful ocean surf, that has turned the title race into one they can win. "Bringing the sport together under one tour was about giving every rider a fair shot at a world title. Taking the tour to the world's great wave venues has brought new contenders like Bernd into the race, and both titles now go down to the final event." - Simeon Glasson - Director - World Windsurf Tour Roediger puts his rise down to simply enjoying his sailing. "For me, I've never had more fun on tour. I haven't done any events where I've felt I'm going to them just for points. To follow your passion and get some results doing that is a pretty cool feeling. Who knows what will happen in the title race, but what got me to this point is just having fun with it." - Bernd Roediger Drama at Ho'okipa Roediger's run to the final was anything but smooth. In his opening heat, in 10 to 15 foot wave faces and light winds, he climbed from fourth to first in the final five minutes. Only the top two in each four-man heat advanced, and a towering last-gasp aerial saved him. "It was very, very challenging and I was super lucky to get that final wave. But then everything started to click and started to feel good." - Bernd Roediger From there he grew stronger. He won his quarter-final with some of the event's most thrilling moments, including one of the top single-wave scores (8.08). He then dominated his semi-final with the highest semi-final score (14.90), highlighted by a tweaked aerial off the main peak. In the final, Roediger led for most of the heat. His best ride, the top score of the final at 7 points, saw him hit the top of a big wave and spin off it into the air for a ‘taka’ move. He added a one-handed aerial and a full 360-degree spin on the wave face for a total of 13.40. But Pare-Rico overtook him in the closing minutes to win by 0.05 points. The title race heads to Chile Roediger arrived in Hawaii fourth in the world rankings, 6,000 points behind leader Marc Pare-Rico of Spain, the reigning world champion. His path improved as two of the sport's most decorated champions fell early. Germany's Philip Köster, a five-time world wave champion ranked second, went out in the quarter-finals. Brazil's Marcilio Browne, a four-time champion ranked third, lost in the semi-finals. Pare-Rico's win gives him a 6,410-point lead. Roediger is now third, 7,500 points behind, heading into the Grand Final in Chile (November 14-29). Under the tour's scoring he is expected to drop a low result from earlier in the season, in Puerto Rico. That means he can still win the world title if he wins in Chile and Pare-Rico finishes outside the top five. More American success Maui's Morgan Noireaux also reached the men's final, snatching the last place with his final two rides. Noireaux, a four-time Aloha Classic winner, finished fourth. In the women's event, former world wave champion Angela Cochrane of the USA finished fourth, using her local knowledge to pick out the best waves. The women's world title will also be decided in Chile. France's Marine Hunter won in Hawaii to cut Germany's Lina Erpenstein's lead from 1,435 points to just 15. ph.title: Evacuees reunite with family at the Ukrainian-Belarusian border after fleeing Oleshky
ph.description: CHERNIHIV REGION, Ukraine (AP) — Residents of Russian-occupied Oleshky crossed into Ukrainian-held territory Saturday in a major evacuation operation carried out under the most significant truce since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine 4½ years ago. Evacuees wrapped in blue and yellow Ukrainian flags stepped off buses at the Ukrainian-Belarusian border and reunited with family members. Volunteers with hand-drawn welcome signs handed out coffee to the weary travelers who had journeyed by bus and plane through Russia and Belarus. Residents of nearby villages lined the highway waving flags and flashlights to greet the convoy. Tetiana Leonidivna, 71, thanked the Ukrainian soldiers who helped her flee. "We love them, we love them," she said through tears. "We know that they are protecting us. And a deep bow to them, and a deep bow to their parents, for having such children. I am proud, I am simply proud." The ceasefire in Ukraine's southern Kherson region began early Tuesday and was expected to continue through Sunday evening. The White House has said U.S. first lady Melania Trump helped to broker the localized truce, while Pope Leo XIV pressed Russia and Ukraine to allow aid deliveries and evacuations. Evacuees and their families express fear and hope Relatives and volunteers with the Red Cross, Doctors Without Borders and World Central Kitchen welcomed the evacuees as they arrived at the border, ready to provide aid and food. Crews unloaded crates of pets — including cats, dogs, a parrot and a raccoon — from the buses. Holding a cigarette between shaking fingers, 48-year-old Ivan Yevhenovych described his last months in Oleshky. "It was very difficult. There were a lot of drones. It was hard to move around the streets," he said. "Since spring, there hasn't really been any staple food left. People had a little bit of their own reserves. We are thrifty people." He said landmines or drone strikes were killing residents every day. An estimated 2,000 people remained in Oleshky when the temporary truce took hold. They were offered the choice of evacuating to territory controlled by Ukraine or Russia, or remaining in the city with replenished food and medical supplies. "Many people stayed behind and didn't want to leave," Yevhenovych said. "Some for their houses, some for their animals." Ukrainian authorities, seeking to protect those who remained and safeguard future humanitarian missions, have not said how many residents were evacuated from Oleshky and have restricted details of their route. Melania Trump posted on social media Friday that the humanitarian convoy could safely evacuate more than 750 people. Liza Paliy, 19, waited at the border for her father, whom she last saw more than 2½ years earlier when she fled the occupied city with her mother and sister. "We thought at that time that it would be a month, two maximum, and we would return, but unfortunately, two years have already passed," she said. Ukraine and Russia plan more humanitarian missions Ukraine's human rights ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, hailed the humanitarian mission as a win. "This is an extremely important moment. Behind us are difficult negotiations, agreements, preparations, and an enormous amount of work. But most importantly, the people who waited so long to be rescued are finally safe," he said in an online post. Lubinets and Yana Lantratova, Russia's human rights commissioner, said in separate statements that the two sides agreed to continue working on similar humanitarian missions. "The mission has concluded, but, unfortunately, living conditions in Oleshky remain extremely difficult," Lantratova said. "We will make every effort to support those residents who have made the decision to stay." Some Oleshky evacuees who chose to move to Russian-occupied territory were taken to a temporary shelter in Simferopol, Lantratova said. Crimea is a Ukrainian peninsula that Russia annexed in 2014. "After everything they have endured and a long journey, it is essential for these people to rest, recover, and feel cared for. However, support should not be limited to just a roof over their heads and a hot meal," she said in a social media post. The US approves Patriot missile sale for Ukraine Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Saturday welcomed U.S. approval of his country's purchase of 500 PAC-3 Patriot interceptors, which are needed to stop Russian ballistic missiles. "Right now, the Russians are attacking our energy infrastructure every single day. In just these past two weeks of October, there have already been more than 30 Russian strikes on critical parts of our power grid," Zelenskyy wrote on X. The Trump administration said Friday it has approved the proposed $2.1 billion sale. It remains subject to congressional review. Additionally, 500 Patriot missiles would be purchased for Ukraine through a U.S. program using donations from Canada, Germany and Norway, the State Department said. Yegor Kovalchuk said Saturday. Five others were wounded, he said. Local officials also reported Ukrainian drone attacks in the Russian republic of Bashkortostan. Russian media outlets said there was a fire in the region's capital, Ufa, home to several oil refineries. The Russian Defense Ministry said Saturday its forces had shot down 433 Ukrainian drones overnight. Zelenskyy said Moscow launched drone attacks on energy and railway infrastructure across Ukraine overnight, leaving 280,000 households in Dnipro and Kyiv regions without power. The attacks targeted combined heat and power plants in Kyiv and Sumy regions, four electricity substations and a gas distribution facility in the Dnipro region and railway infrastructure in Dnipro and Kharkiv, he said, adding that repair crews were working to restore power.
